newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SA GET TIMELY "WAKE-UP CALL"--TEICHMANN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SA GET TIMELY "WAKE-UP CALL"--TEICHMANN.

text.p: Stuttering performances in recent weeks by South African provincial sides in the southern hemisphere's Super 12 competition surprised British Lions manager Fran Cotton on the eve of his squad's departure this Saturday from Lodon.

But, although Cotton said he was not going to be misled by one or two bad weekejds, Springbok captain Gary Teichmann feels these stuttering performances have given the South Africans a timely "wake-up call".

"The fact that some of our sides have gone off the boil a little in the Super 12 has given us a bit of wake-up call - that we're not as good as we make out to be and thAt we must start working together," Teichmann said.
"The Lions are going to be a good side and there's no ways we can sit back and say the northern hemisphere are not up to standard with the southern hemisphere.

"I believe that it's going to be a very hard test series but I believe that we've got the players to win. If we don't have too many injuries and if we can maintain the same sort of core that we had last year, then it'll go well."

After the disappointment last year of losing a home series to New Zealand for the first time in their impressive rugby union history, South Africa bounced back with five successive test wins against Argentina, France and Wales. Teichmann proved to be n inspirational and focused captain who always led from the front.
This year, Teichmann has been in storming form at number eight for his province Natal during the Super 12 and he pinpoints the Lions' forwards as their major strength for the forthcoming series.
"I think their pack is going to be strong - they've got in a couple of their league players and they've got good lineout forwards. So we can expect a very hard tussle up front.

"With their backline players, again they've brought in a few league players who are tough customers. They've adapted to the union game quickly - most of them played union before and then came back, so it's not a big change for them. But, all-round, I hink the Lions will be a good side."
With party grouping together players from the four Home Nations, Teichmann is aware that the initial challenge facing experienced coach Ian McGeechan is to get the appropriate balance off his side.

"That'll be the key factor - if they can sort out their test side from their weekday side and how soon they can get it together. But they're all top players so they should be able to do it fairly quickly.
"What's good for them is that they've got a long period playing against the provincial sides before they play us in the tests so they would have had a few games to sort things out."
